examples: Which song shall we play?
They couldn't decide which song to play.
wiktionary.gloss: What, of those mentioned or implied.

examples: Take which one you want.
You may go which way you please.
wiktionary.gloss: The/Any ... that; whichever.

examples: He once owned a painting of the house, which painting would later be stolen.
She only speaks Chinese, which language I can hardly follow.
wiktionary.gloss: Designates the one(s) previously mentioned.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz. Cognates include Scots whilk (“which”), West Frisian hokker (“which”), Dutch welk (“which”), Low German welk (“which”), German welcher (“which”), Danish hvilken (“which”), Swedish vilken (“which”), Norwegian hvilken (“which”), Icelandic hvílíkur (“which”).

senses.definition: used to ask what one or ones from a limited group of choices

examples.en: Both jackets look great, so which do you prefer?
examples.vi: Cả hai chiếc áo khoác đều đẹp, vậy bạn thích cái nào hơn?

senses.definition: used in a relative clause to refer to things or animals previously mentioned

examples.en: The house, which has four bedrooms, was built in 1990.
examples.vi: Ngôi nhà, cái mà có bốn phòng ngủ, được xây dựng vào năm 1990.

senses.definition: used to refer to an entire situation or fact just described

examples.en: He missed his flight, which caused many problems for the team.
examples.vi: Anh ấy bị lỡ chuyến bay, điều này đã gây ra nhiều rắc rối cho cả đội.

senses.definition: the one or ones that you choose; whichever

examples.en: Here are several designs; choose which you like best.
examples.vi: Đây là vài mẫu thiết kế; hãy chọn cái bạn thích nhất.

examples: Which is which?
By now, you must surely know which is which.
wiktionary.gloss: What one or ones (of those mentioned or implied).

examples: Please take which you please.
wiktionary.gloss: The/Any ones that; whichever.

examples: I dropped a saucepan, which knocked over the eggs, which went all over the kitchen floor.
I found my camera, which I thought I'd lost, under the bed.
wiktionary.gloss: Referring to a preceding noun.

examples: The front door was open, which concerned me.
He had to leave, which was very difficult.
wiktionary.gloss: Referring to a preceding statement.

examples: This is the letter which I received.
This is the letter in which he explains his decision.
wiktionary.gloss: In a restrictive relative clause, referring to a noun previously mentioned.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English which, hwic, wilche, hwilch, whilk, hwilc, from Old English hwelċ (“which”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind”, literally “like what”), derived from *hwaz. Cognates include Scots whilk (“which”), West Frisian hokker (“which”), Dutch welk (“which”), Low German welk (“which”), German welcher (“which”), Danish hvilken (“which”), Swedish vilken (“which”), Norwegian hvilken (“which”), Icelandic hvílíkur (“which”).

wiktionary.gloss: Introduces an anacoluthon.

examples: They only offered me five dollars, which I wouldn’t do it for less than fifteen.
wiktionary.gloss: And.

idioms.gloss: To possess sound judgment or common sense; to have a clear understanding of a situation.
To be confused about how to handle a situation.
idioms.phrase: not know which way to turn

idioms.gloss: Used to ask which transit route reaches a specific location or destination.
To be aware of where one's interests lie in a situation.
idioms.phrase: know which side one's bread is buttered on

idioms.gloss: One does not require an expert to tell one what one already knows.
idioms.phrase: you don't need a weatherman to know which way the wind blows

idioms.gloss: To delay taking action based on the outcome of something else.
idioms.phrase: see which way the cat jumps

idioms.gloss: Which point of view is considered or whose interests are used as a basis.
idioms.phrase: which foot the shoe is on

idioms.gloss: One must give something (especially taxes) owed to the relevant authority.
idioms.phrase: render unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's
